introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION (GCE) BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0750 Geography 1, JUNE 2021, ADVANCED LEVEL. Multiple choice question paper, one hour 30 minutes. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Instructions to candidates: use a soft HB pencil throughout the examination; do not open the booklet until told to do so; check that the booklet is headed 'Advanced Level - 0750 Geography 1'. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is correct, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question: if you mark more than one answer you will score a zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question; you can come back to it later. Do all rough work in the booklet, using the blank spaces. Calculators are allowed. The paper has two sections: Section A, Physical Geography (questions 1 to 25), and Section B, Human Geography (questions 26 to 50).

questions.enonce_markdown: The atmospheric layer which has the highest concentration of gases is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The atmosphere is densest at the surface and thins out with height, so the layer touching the ground holds most of the gas. The troposphere (from the surface to roughly 8-16 km depending on latitude) contains about three quarters of the mass of the atmosphere and nearly all of its water vapour, dust and weather. The stratosphere, mesosphere and thermosphere lie above it and are progressively thinner.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The graph below shows the *pattern of global heat Energy budget.* Why is there a positive energy budget between latitudes 0° and 35° N and south of the equator?

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

Fig. 1: Pattern of global heat energy budget
questions.corrige_markdown:
On the graph the curve of net shortwave (incoming solar) radiation lies above the curve of net longwave (outgoing) radiation between about 35° N and 35° S, which gives a **surplus**; poleward of about 35° the longwave loss is larger, which gives a **deficit**. The surplus energy is carried towards the higher latitudes by the atmosphere and the oceans (the arrows on the figure).

The *cause* of the surplus is the **high angle of incidence** of the sun's rays in the low latitudes: the rays are almost vertical, so a given beam of energy is concentrated on a small surface and crosses a shorter path through the atmosphere, so less is lost by absorption and scattering. Near the poles the angle is low, the energy is spread over a larger area and the deficit appears (option D is the reason for the deficit, not the surplus). Options B and C only describe the position; they do not explain why the budget is positive.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The high angle of incidence of the sun's rays
The location close to the equator
The location further away from the poles
The low angle of incidence of the sun's rays

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following statements best defines dew point?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The dew point is a **temperature**: the temperature to which air must be cooled, at constant pressure and moisture content, for it to become saturated (relative humidity 100 %). Cooled below that temperature, the excess water vapour condenses into liquid droplets (dew, fog, cloud). Options A and C describe a height (the condensation level), not a temperature, and option B describes a place.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: The altitude at which clouds begin to form
The location where dew easily forms on the surface
The height at which condensation begins in the atmosphere
The temperature at which air becomes saturated and excess vapour becomes liquid

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following climatic characteristics are similar between the Equatorial Climate and the Tropical Monsoon Climate?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Both climates lie in the low latitudes. Both have **high temperatures** all year (monthly means well above 18 °C, with a small annual range) and **heavy rainfall** (annual totals of the order of 1500 mm or more). What differs is the *distribution* of the rain (well spread over the year in the equatorial climate, concentrated in a long wet season with a short dry season in the monsoon climate) and above all the **winds**: the monsoon climate is defined by a seasonal reversal of the winds, whereas equatorial winds are light and variable (the doldrums). So options B and D, which include wind, are wrong. The textbook comparison is made on temperature and rainfall.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following towns in Cameroon shows a yearly rainfall graph with a single maximum?

*Options as printed:* A) Sangmalima   B) Yaounde   C) Bamenda   D) Douala
questions.corrige_markdown:
A rainfall graph with a single maximum (monomodal regime) belongs to the Cameroon-type climate: one long rainy season with a peak in July-September. Sangmelima and Yaounde, in the southern plateau, have the Guinean/equatorial regime with **two** rainy seasons and two maxima (March-June and September-November) separated by a short dry spell in July-August. Bamenda (Western Highlands) and Douala (coast) both have a single rainy season with one peak in about August, so **both C and D fit the question**; the printed question therefore has no unique key.

**Intended answer: C (Bamenda) or D (Douala), both fit.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The more permanent water below the water table is called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The water table is the upper surface of the zone of saturation. Below it all pores and cracks are filled with water, which is the more permanent store of groundwater: it is called **phreatic water**. Vadose water is the water held in the unsaturated zone above the water table, and meteoric water is water of atmospheric origin (rain, snow). "Underground water" is a general term for any water below the surface, not the specific name for the permanent saturated store.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 2 below shows the influence of basin size on the shape of the storm hydrograph. Why would a small basin produce a sharp peak hydrograph?

![fig-2](gce-al-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

Figure 2: Relationship between basin size and lag time
questions.corrige_markdown:
On the graph the small basin has a short lag time (the interval between peak rainfall and peak discharge) and a steep, high, narrow peak, while the large basin has a long lag time and a low, broad peak. In a small basin all the places where rain falls are **close to the main stream**, so the runoff from every part of the basin reaches the channel at almost the same time and the discharge rises quickly to a sharp peak. In a large basin the water comes from far away at different times, so the arrival is spread out and the peak is flattened. Slope (option D) also matters but does not explain the *size* effect shown on the figure.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Possible sources of water are scattered from the main stream
Possible sources of water are closer to the main stream
Possible sources of water are equal in all directions
Possible sources of water run over steep slopes

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the mean bifurcation ratio of the stream below?

![fig-3](gce-al-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

Fig. 3: Stream network
questions.corrige_markdown:
The bifurcation ratio is $R_b = \dfrac{N_u}{N_{u+1}}$, the number of streams of one order divided by the number of the next higher order.

Count on the figure (Strahler orders): 4 streams of order 1, 2 streams of order 2, 1 stream of order 3.

- $R_{b}(1\text{-}2) = 4/2 = 2$
- $R_{b}(2\text{-}3) = 2/1 = 2$

Mean bifurcation ratio $= (2 + 2)/2 = 2.00$ (the same value is obtained by weighting each ratio by the number of streams involved). The other options come from miscounting the segments.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What name is given to the layer of the earth which lies below the lithosphere, where seismic waves decrease with distance?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The lithosphere (crust plus the rigid uppermost mantle) rests on the **asthenosphere**, a hot, weak, partly molten part of the upper mantle that flows slowly. Seismic waves slow down in it (it is the "low-velocity zone"), which is how it was identified. Continental and oceanic crust are parts of the lithosphere itself, and a plate is a slab of lithosphere.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The type of plate margin between the African and Eurasian plate is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The African plate is moving northwards and pushing against the Eurasian plate, so the two plates converge. Where continental crust meets continental crust neither plate is easily subducted, and the crust is crumpled and uplifted: this is a **collision margin**, of which the Alps (and the Mediterranean belt of fold mountains) are the classic result. A constructive margin is a divergent one (new crust, as on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge) and a conservative margin is one where plates slide past each other (San Andreas fault).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is an earthquake event considered a hazard?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A natural hazard is a natural event that threatens people and their property. An earthquake is a hazard because its shaking, ground rupture, landslides and tsunamis **can cause loss of life and destroy buildings and infrastructure** (option D). That the event cannot be controlled (A) or occurs mainly at plate margins (C) is true but does not make it a hazard; option B is close but speaks only of danger to humans and omits property, so D is the most complete statement.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Earthquakes are potential danger to humans
Earthquakes occur mainly at plate margins
An earthquake can cause loss of life and property

questions.enonce_markdown: It is more rugged and mountainous with many high volcanic peaks and high altitude plains. This is a description of which relief region in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Western Highlands of Cameroon (the Bamenda and Bamileke highlands, Mount Oku and neighbouring peaks, along the Cameroon Volcanic Line) are rugged, volcanic, and contain high plateaux. The Southern Low Plateau is an undulating plateau of about 500-700 m, the coastal lowlands are low and flat, and the northern lowlands (Benue and Chad basins) are low-lying plains.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which of the following areas do you expect to find deep chemical weathering?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Chemical weathering (hydrolysis, oxidation, solution) needs **both heat and water**, because reaction rates roughly double for each 10 °C rise and water is the reactant. Humid tropical climates provide both all year, with abundant organic acids from the forest, so weathering profiles (regolith) reach tens of metres in depth. Hot deserts lack water, cold and polar climates lack heat, and wet and dry continental climates are only partly favourable.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A constructive sea wave is one where?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A constructive wave is a low, long wave that breaks gently with a strong **swash** and a weak backwash. It carries sediment up the beach and leaves it there, so it builds up (constructs) the beach. When the backwash is stronger than the swash, the wave is destructive and removes material from the beach.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Backwash and swash erode and deposit beach material

questions.enonce_markdown: The following processes are associated with the work of streams: suspension, solution, traction, saltation. These can best be summarized as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Suspension, solution, traction and saltation are the four ways in which a river moves its load: fine particles are carried in suspension, dissolved material in solution, and coarser particles are rolled along the bed by traction or bounced by saltation. They are therefore all **transportational** processes (erosion is by abrasion, hydraulic action, attrition and corrosion; deposition happens when the river loses energy).

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the type of mass movement shown in the picture below (fig. 4).

![fig-4](gce-al-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

Fig. 4: A type of mass movement
questions.corrige_markdown:
The photograph shows a grassy slope with **curved (crescent-shaped) back scarps** and the displaced material forming steps below them: blocks of soil have moved down a concave slip surface and rotated slightly backwards. That is **slumping** (rotational slip), common on clay or weathered slopes that are saturated and undercut. Soil creep is slow and shows only tiny terracettes and tilted posts; a landslide is a fast, mostly planar slide of a large mass; a mudflow is a fluid flow of saturated debris with a tongue-like lobe.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The four types of humus in the soil are
questions.corrige_markdown:
Humus, the dark, well-decomposed organic part of the soil, is classified into **mull** (mild, well mixed with the mineral soil, in fertile, active soils), **moder** (intermediate), **mor** (acid raw humus, in cool, wet coniferous or heath conditions) and **peat** (accumulated, poorly decomposed in waterlogged conditions). Option B lists the four components of a soil, not types of humus, and "organic matter" in A and C is not a type of humus.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Organic matter, mor, moder and peat
Mineral, organic matter, water and air
Mull, organic matter, moder and peat

questions.enonce_markdown: In Jenney's Equation, S=f(Cl,O,R,P,T): Which of the soil forming factors do you consider the most influential?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Jenny's equation soil (S) is a function of climate (Cl), organisms (O), relief (R), parent material (P) and time (T). Climate is generally regarded as the **most influential** factor because temperature and rainfall control the rate of weathering and leaching, the amount of vegetation and humus, and the activity of soil organisms, and they explain the broad world pattern of zonal soils. Parent material and relief act more locally; time only allows the other factors to operate.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: It is a characteristic of soil development in the Tropical rainforest region?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the hot, wet tropical rainforest, intense chemical weathering and leaching remove silica and bases and leave a residue of iron and aluminium oxides: this is **ferrallitisation** (the process producing red ferrallitic soils, or ferralsols). Calcification occurs in semi-arid grasslands, podzolisation in cool, wet coniferous forests, and salinisation in hot, dry areas with strong evaporation.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In which of the following categories will you classify the volcanic soils of the Mount Cameroon area and the alluvials on the Coastal lowlands?

*Options as printed:* A) Azonal soils   B) Zonal soils   C) Intrazonal soils   D) Fertile soils
questions.corrige_markdown:
Zonal soils reflect the regional climate and vegetation (for example ferrallitic soils of the equatorial forest). Soils of the Mount Cameroon area and the coastal alluvial plains owe their character mainly to **local factors**, the parent material (recent volcanic ash and lava, river deposits), rather than to climate. The textbook category for soils dominated by local parent material or drainage is **intrazonal**. However, young volcanic and alluvial soils with little profile development are also described as azonal in some classifications, so options A and C are both defensible and the printed key is not unique.

**Intended answer: intrazonal soils (C); azonal soils (A) is also defensible.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Animals that feed upon mixed diet of plants and animals are called:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Animals that eat both plants and animals are **omnivores** (humans, pigs, chimpanzees). Autotrophs make their own food (green plants), and carnivores eat only animals. (Options B and D are printed identically in the paper; neither is correct, so the key is unaffected.)

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A degraded climax vegetation that has been maintained for long in an area due to persistent human interference is known as
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **plagioclimax** (or deflected climax) is a plant community held at a stage different from the natural climax by long-continued human activity such as grazing, burning or cultivation (for example the savanna maintained by repeated bush fires in the forest zone). A monoclimax is the single climax controlled by climate in the monoclimax theory, a subclimax is a stage short of the climax maintained by natural factors, and a polyclimax is one of several climaxes controlled by local factors.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the ecosystem or biome with the least Net Primary Productivity (NPP) from the following:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Net primary productivity is the amount of organic matter produced by plants per unit area and time, after respiration. It is highest in the tropical rainforest (selva), which has heat, abundant water and year-round growth; it is lower in the savanna, lower again in the boreal forest (short, cold growing season), and **lowest in the tropical desert**, where lack of water and sparse vegetation limit photosynthesis.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Once a lot of deforestation takes place, there is an imbalance in global oxygen and carbon dioxide leading to the accumulation of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere. This contributes most significantly to;
questions.corrige_markdown:
Trees absorb carbon dioxide in photosynthesis, and burning or rotting cleared forest releases it. More CO$_2$ in the air strengthens the greenhouse effect, which traps more outgoing long-wave radiation and so contributes to **global warming**. Ozone depletion is caused mainly by CFCs, and solar radiation reaching the top of the atmosphere is not changed by CO$_2$. Erosion increases after deforestation but is not the effect of the accumulated carbon dioxide.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Building levees and retaining walls, construction of dams, straightening meanders are some of the ways to control:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Levees and retaining walls contain the river inside its channel, dams store flood water, and straightening meanders (channelisation) speeds the flow out of the area. All are **engineering methods of flood control**.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following assertions is incorrect?
questions.corrige_markdown:
World population is very unevenly distributed: most people live near the coasts, on low ground, and in the temperate and subtropical latitudes of the **Northern Hemisphere**, where most of the land lies. About 90 % of people live north of the equator, so the statement that over 60 % live in the Southern Hemisphere is **incorrect**. The other three assertions follow the usual textbook generalisations (concentration near the sea, on low land, and in the northern middle latitudes), although the exact percentages vary between sources.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: 75% of the world population lives within 1000km from the sea.
Over 60% of the world population lives in the Southern Hemisphere.
85% of the world population lives in areas less than 500m high.
85% of the world population lives between latitude 20°N and 68°N of the Equator.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is an economic consequence of the second stage of the Demographic Transition Model?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In stage 2 (early expanding) the birth rate stays high while the death rate falls, so the population grows quickly. In a poor, mainly agrarian economy this growth places heavy pressure on resources and services and keeps **income per head low**: that is the *economic* consequence. Low literacy is social, high life expectancy is demographic (and it rises in stage 2 for demographic reasons), and high transport development is characteristic of the later stages when the economy has developed.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following examples would John consider as a "Push factor" as he considers moving from Maroua to Kribi by 2017?

*Options as printed:* A) Harsh climate condition   B) Hunger   C) High crime wave   D) Large majority of the people are not Christians
questions.corrige_markdown:
A push factor is a negative condition at the place of origin which drives people away. Maroua, in the Far North Region, has a hot, dry Sudano-Sahelian climate with a long dry season and droughts, so **harsh climatic conditions** are a push factor from there (Kribi, on the humid coast, offers a very different climate). However, hunger and a high crime wave are also push factors in general, and the religion statement could be one for some people, so the item has more than one defensible answer.

**Intended answer: A (harsh climate condition); hunger and a high crime wave are also push factors.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the characteristics of a country below and answer the question that follows.

- High level of unemployment
- Diminishing returns to factors of production
- High population densities
- Low living standards

This country is said to be:-
questions.corrige_markdown:
Overpopulation exists when there are too many people for the available resources and technology, so that living standards fall below what they could be. The listed signs (unemployment, **diminishing returns** as more labour is added to a fixed amount of land and capital, high density, low living standards) are exactly the signs of an **over-populated** country. An under-populated country would have labour shortage and increasing returns, and an optimum population has the highest standard of living. "Under developed" describes the level of development, not the balance between people and resources.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A country with a population of 5 million and with 50,000 births per year has a crude birth rate of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Crude birth rate $= \dfrac{\text{births in a year}}{\text{total population}} \times 1000 = \dfrac{50\,000}{5\,000\,000} \times 1000 = 10$ per 1000.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A country's population is expected to rise and its average age is expected to fall in future. Which of the following is likely to cause this?
questions.corrige_markdown:
For the total population to rise, more people must be added than are lost, and for the average age to fall the added people must be young. A **rising birth rate** adds babies, and **net immigration** brings in mainly young adults (and their children). A falling birth rate and net emigration (often of young adults) would lower the total and raise the average age.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Birth rate decreases; migration: net emigration
Birth rate decreases; migration: net immigration
Birth rate increases; migration: net emigration
Birth rate increases; migration: net immigration

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a positive impact of greying or ageing population?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A greying population creates costs (higher pension and health bills, larger public spending on the elderly) and a shrinking labour force. The one **positive** effect among the options is that a labour shortage pushes firms to invest in machines, so there is **greater technological development and automation** in production.

**Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Increase in pension bills since there are many old persons.
Increased government expenditure to cater for the old
Shortage in labour supply especially for intensive labour jobs
Greater technological development in production (automation systems)

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following most accurately defines intensive farming?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Intensive farming uses **large inputs** (labour, capital, fertiliser, irrigation) on a **relatively small area** to obtain a **high yield** per hectare. Option A has small inputs, B describes monoculture, and D describes extensive commercial farming (large capital on a vast area).

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: A farming system where by a farmer uses small amounts of input on a small piece of land to obtain high output.
A farming system whereby only one type of crop is grown on the total surface area.
A farming system where by a farmer uses large amount of input on a relatively small piece of land to obtain high output.
A farming system where by a farmer uses large amounts of capital on vast land to obtain high output.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study Fig. 5 below which shows the economic rent curves for the location of three crops A, B and C.

![fig-5](gce-al-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

Figure 5: Economic Rent curves

Point N on the diagram represents:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In von Thunen's model each crop has an economic-rent line that falls with distance from the market. Near the market (left) the crop with the highest rent (A) is grown; at the distance where the line of one crop crosses the line of the next, both give the same rent and land use changes from one crop to the other. On the figure the vertical line N is drawn through the intersection of the lines of B and C: it is the **margin of transference**, where cultivation switches from crop B to crop C. The **margin of cultivation** (limit of cultivation) is the point where a rent line reaches zero on the distance axis.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: According to Alfred Weber, lines that join places with equal transport cost for moving either raw materials or finished products are known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
In Weber's theory of industrial location, **isotims** are lines joining points of equal transport cost for moving a raw material or the finished product to or from a given point. **Isodapanes** join points of equal *additional* transport cost (deviation from the least-cost location). Isophores is not a Weberian term and "isolines" is a general word for any line of equal value.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the pair representing the major human factors that influence the distribution of farming systems in Cameroon.

*Options as printed:* A) Population and transport network   B) Cultural and demographic factors   C) Transport network and market   D) Government policy and relief
questions.corrige_markdown:
Human (as opposed to physical) factors in the distribution of farming include market, transport, population density, culture and government policy. Option D is eliminated because relief is physical. In the classical location approach (von Thunen) the **market** and the **transport network** (cost of reaching the market) are the main human factors, which makes C the usual textbook answer. But A and B are also pairs of human factors, so the printed question has no unique key.

**Intended answer: C (transport network and market), the classical von Thunen factors; A and B are also defensible.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Name the type of network illustrated on the diagram below (Fig. 6).

![fig-6](gce-al-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)

Fig. 6: Type of transport network
questions.corrige_markdown:
The diagram joins five nodes (A to E) by many links forming several **closed loops** (for example A-B-C, A-C-E, B-C-D), with more than one route between most pairs of nodes. That is a **circuit network**, the most developed type of transport network, typical of well-developed areas. A branching network has no loops (one route between two points, as in a tree), and a travelling-salesman network is a single route visiting every node once. "Paul reverse" is not a recognised network type (probably a misprint).

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
When a barge stops in Douala, unloads its cargo, and transfers it onto a train to be transported to Yaounde. Douala is referred to as:

*Options as printed:* A) Break of bulk   B) Break of bulk   C) Export - processing zone   D) Trading bloc
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **break of bulk** point is a place where goods are transferred from one mode of transport to another (here from ship or barge to rail), which is what a port like Douala does. An export-processing zone is an area producing goods for export under special conditions, and a trading bloc is a group of countries with trade agreements. Options A and B are printed identically in the paper, so a letter cannot be chosen between them.

**Intended answer: break of bulk (option A or B, printed identically).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The growth of woodwork industries such as COCAM and ECAM-PLACAGE in Mbalmayo and other related factories can be best explained by the factor of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Mbalmayo lies in the southern forest zone, close to timber resources. Wood processing (sawing, veneer and plywood) is a weight-losing, bulky-material industry, so it is cheaper to process the logs near the forest than to carry them far. The factor is **nearness to the raw material (timber)**.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 7 shows an agricultural system with inputs, processes and outputs.

![fig-7](gce-al-geography-2021-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)

Fig. 7: Agriculture as a system

Identify the agricultural system
questions.corrige_markdown:
The diagram uses the sizes of the boxes to show the scale of each component: the **land** box is small, while the **inputs** box is relatively large and the **outputs** box is the largest. A small area receiving large inputs and giving a large output is the definition of **intensive** farming, and an output larger than the input (a surplus sold for profit) indicates **commercial** farming. So the system shown is an intensive commercial one. Extensive systems would show a large land box with small inputs.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one determines hill site location of settlements on the Mandara mountain in Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the Mandara Mountains of the Far North, settlements of the hill peoples were built high on the slopes and ridges mainly for **defence**: the heights were easy to protect against raiders and invasions in the past, and the steep rocky sites were hard to attack. Climate, farming and tourism are not the original reason for the hill sites.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following settlement forms is likely to develop in a constricted valley?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a narrow (constricted) valley the flat land is a thin strip, so houses are built one behind another along the valley floor or the road and the river. The result is a long, narrow **ribbon (linear) settlement**. A ring form develops around a feature such as a lake, a cruciform at a crossroads, and dispersed settlements are scattered farms.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A rural settlement form in which houses are constructed around a central place left for tribal meetings, communal life or some other reasons.
questions.corrige_markdown:
An **open space village** is a nucleated village whose houses surround a central open area that is kept for meetings, ceremonies, markets or a common purpose (the village square or the chief's place). A clustered settlement is a general term for houses grouped close together without that central space, double villages are two villages facing each other across a road or river, and elongated villages stretch along a line.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: "It is the process of movement of population, industries shopping complexes and offices from the inner city location to the peripheries" which of the following concepts best suits this definition
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Suburbanisation** is the outward movement of people, and then of industries, shopping centres and offices, from the inner city to the suburbs on the edge of the urban area. De-urbanisation is the decline of urban populations or movement back to the countryside, re-urbanisation is the return of people and activities to the city centre, and decentralisation is the wider (often planned) spreading of activities away from the centre.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A situation in a country where two cities dominate the rest in terms of wealth, economic activities and services is known as:-
questions.corrige_markdown:
When **two** cities dominate the urban system of a country (for example Douala and Yaounde in Cameroon) the pattern is called **binary**. A primate pattern is dominated by a single city, a stepped-order pattern shows distinct size groups, and the rank-size rule is a regularity linking the size of a city to its rank.

**Answer: B.**
themes: urban hierarchy and rank size rule

questions.enonce_markdown: Referring to the rank size rule, what is the relationship between the size of settlements and their rank?
questions.corrige_markdown:
According to the rank-size rule, the population of the city of rank $n$ is about $1/n$ of the population of the largest city, so as the rank number increases the population decreases: the relationship is **inverse (negative)**.

**Answer: B.**
themes: urban hierarchy and rank size rule

questions.enonce_markdown: Using the rank size rule by George Zipf, what is the population of the 3rd largest city, if the largest city has a population of 12 million inhabitants?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rank-size rule: $P_n = \dfrac{P_1}{n}$. For the third city: $P_3 = \dfrac{12\,000\,000}{3} = 4\,000\,000$.

**Answer: B.**
themes: urban hierarchy and rank size rule

questions.enonce_markdown: One of the following soil conservation method is least practiced in Cameroon. Which is the one?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Stone lines and terracing are traditional methods used on slopes in the Far North (Mandara Mountains) and the Western Highlands, and the use of farm additives (manure, compost, fertiliser) is widespread. **Strip cultivation**, which needs fairly large, mechanised fields with strips of different crops following the contour, is the one rarely practised by Cameroonian smallholders. The question is a matter of regional knowledge and D is the best-supported answer.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a negative impact of globalisation?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Globalisation exposes local workers to competition from imports and to the relocation of firms, so jobs become less secure (**employment uncertainty**), which is a negative effect. A larger market share, greater interdependence and integration, and solidarity and cohesion are presented as benefits.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following best describes multi-lateral aid to countries?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Multilateral aid** is given by several donor countries who pool funds in an international organisation (for example the World Bank, UN agencies, the African Development Bank), which then distributes it to the recipients. Bilateral aid goes directly from one government to another, so options A and B describe bilateral aid and option D is not the usual definition.

**Answer: C.**
